entry.title: feat: show dictionary cards open and leave collapsing to dictionaries…
entry.content:
feat: show dictionary cards open and leave collapsing to dictionaries (#115) (#117)

#112 wrapped every dictionary card in a closed `details` behind a large solid
`▶`/`▼` marker, so every lookup needed a click per dictionary before a
definition could be read, and dictionaries that already ship their own
disclosures (Bee's Ultimate Grammar Dictionary's per-source blocks) needed two.

Follow Yomitan instead. A dictionary card is a plain `div` with a
non-interactive title, and its definitions are always shown. Only
structured-content `details` a dictionary authors collapse: closed unless the
entry sets `open: true`, and styled as Yomitan styles `gloss-sc-details` /
`gloss-sc-summary` -- a 1.4em indent with the native marker hanging outside.
A dictionary's own scoped styles still override this.

Back restores every remaining disclosure's saved state again. The live
display-name refresh now targets the card title instead of `details > summary`,
which would otherwise have stopped renaming cards.

The test harness no longer auto-opens cards. The collapsed-marker e2e check is
replaced by one asserting cards render open with no disclosure control, and
the smoke checks assert open cards and exact restoration of authored details.

  also fails on untouched main
node test/chrome-e2e.mjs -- 192/193, the failure is the pre-existing
  deinflection Note-button assertion noted in #112

entry.title: feat: render dictionary cards collapsed behind an obvious marker (#112)
entry.content:
feat: render dictionary cards collapsed behind an obvious marker (#112)

Dictionary cards were created with `details.open = true` and their disclosure
marker was a 12px `▸` at 0.65 opacity in the muted title colour, so nothing in
the card read as a control: the definitions were simply always there and the
marker was effectively invisible.

Every outer card now renders closed, and the marker is a solid `▶` (`▼` open),
16px in a 20px slot, at full opacity in the theme foreground. Native
`details`/`summary` still does all the work: no custom keyboard handling,
animation or extra header decoration, and `display: list-item` with the native
marker suppressed is unchanged.

Back deliberately resets the outer cards to closed instead of reopening what was
expanded, so returning to a view is the same collapsed starting point as a fresh
lookup. Everything else it restores is untouched -- tab, Show more, scroll,
highlight, toolbar, lazy IPA, and the disclosures a dictionary authored inside a
card body.

Because a collapsed card has no laid-out body, `popupReader` opens the cards it
finds before every read, which is what a reader does to see a definition at all.
The collapsed render is observed through `autoExpandCards: false` readers in the
new marker assertion and in the Back assertion, and in the jsdom renderer checks.

entry.title: Package the scene backgrounds as cropped WebP (12.8 MiB → 0.93 MiB) (…
entry.content:
Package the scene backgrounds as cropped WebP (12.8 MiB → 0.93 MiB) (#111)

* perf: package the scene backgrounds as cropped WebP

The six visual novel frames were owner-supplied 1672x941 PNGs costing 13.1 MB
of the extension, and the scene never showed their bottom quarter: the cover
layer was 140% of the scene height precisely to push each frame's baked-in
dialogue box out of view.

Package the top 1672x672 of every frame - the part the scene displays - as
WebP, and let the cover layer be the scene itself. All six now cost 0.93 MB.

Rendering is unchanged: cover picks scale max(W/1672, 1.4H/941) for the old
pair and max(W/1672, H/672) for the new one, which are the same scale, with the
same center-top anchor.

* docs: record the packaged form of the supplied backgrounds

The ownership record said the supplied PNGs were kept byte-for-byte. They are
now packaged as the cropped WebP the scene displays, so record both: the
supplied files with their original dimensions and checksums as provenance, and
the packaged files with theirs.

* docs: cite the commit that holds all six supplied PNGs

4abbcd3 is where the six files carry the sizes and checksums this record
documents; 1e1a6bf is past ImgBot's lossless re-compression, so an audit
against it would mismatch every hash.

entry.title: feat: install Bee's Ultimate Grammar Dictionary as a default (#110)
entry.content:
feat: install Bee's Ultimate Grammar Dictionary as a default (#110)

Adds a fifth entry to the recommended catalogue, so first-run setup installs a
grammar dictionary alongside the terms, names, kanji and frequency ones. A
visual-novel and manga reader that can define every word in a sentence but not
the grammar joining them leaves the reader to guess at the part that carries the
meaning.

The catalogue already does all the work: every install path, retry path, trust
check and idempotency layer iterates the array. The dictionary is fetched from
its GitHub release like three of the four existing entries, not vendored — this
repo ships no dictionary data, and a ~6MB zip in git would fight the
architecture.

Publisher side was made to satisfy `assertRecommendedDictionary` before this:
the release's `index.json` now declares `indexUrl`, `downloadUrl` and
`isUpdatable`, and `dist/index.json` is published on the default branch. Both
URLs were verified live, and the release-asset redirect resolves under repository
id 1363159785 as `managed-dictionary-source.js` requires.

AGENTS.md's "exact four recommended sources" line is amended in the same commit:
adding a fifth default contradicts it, so the contract moves with the change
rather than being silently violated.

Two test harnesses hardcoded the catalogue size and are now catalogue-derived.
Both were latent bugs, not cosmetic: each drove a wait condition
(`Finished 4 of 4 recommended dictionaries`) that a fifth source can never
satisfy, so the wait degraded into a timeout and every later measurement was
taken mid-flight instead of at the settled state. One of them also ran its
predicate inside `page.waitForFunction`, where the Node-side catalogue does not
exist, so the count is passed in as an argument.

Checks run, with exact outcomes:

* `node test/make-fixture.mjs` — ok
* `node test/node-smoke.mjs` — ok
* `node test/extension-smoke.mjs` — 476 passed, 0 failed
* `node --test test/setup-installer.test.mjs` — 7 pass, 0 fail
* `node --test test/setup-state.test.mjs` — 0 fail
* `node test/chrome-e2e.mjs` — 191/192 checks passed
* `node test/chrome-fallback.mjs` — exit 0

Two failures are pre-existing on `main` and untouched by this change, verified by
re-running both against a clean stash: `chrome-e2e`'s "deinflection disclosure
exposes the real ordered trace" (191/192 on main as well), and
`test/submodule-identity.mjs`, whose pinned gitlink `ed95772` sits behind the tip
of its declared `perf/threaded-import` branch. No submodule is moved here.

No manifest change is needed: `host_permissions` is already `<all_urls>`, the CSP
constrains only `script-src`/`object-src`, and the existing GitHub-release
downloads prove the shape in the real-Chrome suite.
